interest: Reveals Cold War anti-communist screening and diplomatic efforts establishing democratic higher education in occupied Japan.
overview: This file comprises State Department despatches, memoranda, and correspondence from 1948 to 1949 concerning postwar Japanese higher education reforms under the Allied Occupation. A central focus is the establishment, promotion, and fundraising for the International Christian University in Japan, led by Joseph C. Grew and Ralph Diffendorfer, emphasizing democratic principles and anti-communist faculty screening. Additionally, the collection documents discussions with Tokyo University President Shigeru Nambara on university decentralization and diplomatic reorganization, alongside Department inquiries regarding the credentials of Ibaraki Christian College.
